## Contents

-   The Methods–Results **mirror**
-   Where data live: **text vs table vs figure**
-   Reporting a result **fully**
-   Tables & figures **by design**
-   Activities · Checklist

. . .

<br>

> *"Methods was the recipe. Results is the dish."*

## Yesterday's recipe, today's dish

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 10
%%| fig-height: 3
%%| fig-responsive: true
flowchart LR
  I[Introduction] --> M[Methods] --> R[Results] --> D[Discussion]
```

-   **M** — *what you did* ← Day 1
-   **R** — *what you found* ← **this session**

. . .

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
Results is where residents either **over-cook** (interpretation) or **under-plate** (data dump).
:::

## Results must mirror Methods, paragraph for paragraph

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Methods**

1.  Study design
2.  Variables & measurements
3.  Primary analysis
4.  Subgroups / sensitivity
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Results**

1.  → Participant flow
2.  → Table 1
3.  → Primary outcome
4.  → Subgroups / sensitivity
:::
:::::

. . .

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Lay the two sections side by side — they should **reflect**. Anything in Results not set up in Methods is a red flag.
:::

:::{.aside}
Kotz & Cals, J Clin Epidemiol 2013; Enago Academy.
:::

## By the end you can structure, decide, and report {.smaller}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
### Objectives
1.  **Structure** Results to mirror Methods
2.  **Decide** — text vs table vs figure
3.  **Report** stats fully — effect + CI + exact *P*
4.  **Match** figure type to study design
:::

. . .

Objective **3** is the commonest reviewer complaint on Indian submissions; objective **4** separates a generic paper from a design-literate one.

# Block 1 {.inverse background-color="#1f5560"}

### Structuring Results & deciding where data live

## The first Results paragraph is always participant flow

::::: columns
::: {.column width="55%"}
-   Paragraph 1 = **who is in the analysis**
-   Screened → eligible → enrolled → analysed
-   Account for **every** participant
-   Losses & exclusions, **with reasons**
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 4
%%| fig-height: 4
flowchart TD
  S[Screened] --> E[Eligible]
  E --> EN[Enrolled]
  EN --> AN[Analysed]
  E -. excluded .-> X1[ ]
  EN -. lost .-> X2[ ]
```
:::
:::::

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
RCT → **CONSORT** flow · observational → **STROBE** flow · diagnostic → **STARD** flow. The diagram changes; the principle does not.
:::

:::{.aside}
CONSORT 2010 Item 13a · STROBE Item 13 · STARD 2015 Item 19.
:::

## Every finding gets exactly one home — no triple-dipping

::::: columns
::: {.column width="33%"}
::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
### TEXT
headlines, ≤ 3 numbers
:::
:::

::: {.column width="33%"}
::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
### TABLE
many exact numbers
:::
:::

::: {.column width="33%"}
::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
### FIGURE
patterns, trends, time
:::
:::
:::::

. . .

Then **cross-reference** — never repeat. *"Anaemia was the commonest morbidity (Table 2)."*

::: {.important}
The same numbers in a sentence, a table, **and** a chart inflates length and signals inexperience.
:::

:::{.aside}
ICMJE Recommendations · AMA Manual of Style · Enago · Editage.
:::

## Read precisely → table · see instantly → figure · headline → text {.smaller}

| Data scenario | Best home |
|:---|:---|
| One key number (a single prevalence / effect) | **Text** |
| Baseline characteristics, many variables × groups | **Table** |
| Participant flow (screened → analysed) | **Figure** (flow) |
| Time-to-event / survival | **Figure** (K–M) |
| Spread of a continuous variable | **Figure** (box/dot, **not** bar) |
| Many exact estimates readers may re-use | **Table** |

. . .

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
**Numbers to read precisely → table. Patterns to see instantly → figure. Headlines → text. Nothing lives in two homes.**
:::

:::{.aside}
Synthesis of ICMJE · AMA · SAMPL · Weissgerber 2015 · Tufte.
:::

## A complete result has direction, magnitude, precision, and exact *P*

<br>

> **RR 0.66 (95% CI 0.48–0.91); *P* = 0.01**

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
-   **Direction** — which way ✓
-   **Magnitude** — how much ✓
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
-   **Precision** — the 95% CI ✓
-   **Exact *P*** — 0.01, not "< 0.05" ✓
:::
:::::

. . .

::: {.important}
*P* is the **adjunct**; the CI is the message. Never *"P = 0.000"* → report **P < 0.001**. AMA drops the leading zero → *P* = .01.
:::

:::{.aside}
SAMPL (Lang & Altman) · Greenland et al., Eur J Epidemiol 2016 · AMA 11th ed.
:::

## Three sentences a reviewer will flag {.smaller}

::: panel-tabset
### Data dump

❌ *"The mean age was 42.3 years, 58% male, 31% smokers, 22% diabetic, 40% hypertensive, 18% CKD, BMI 26.4, HbA1c 7.8%…"*

::: {.fragment}
✅ *"Participants had a mean age of 42 years and were predominantly male (58%); cardiometabolic comorbidity was common (Table 1)."*
:::

### Interpretation creep

❌ *"Mortality was higher in the control arm **because** dexamethasone suppresses the harmful inflammatory cascade."*

::: {.fragment}
✅ *"28-day mortality was lower in the dexamethasone arm (22.9% vs 25.7%)."* — mechanism is **Discussion**.
:::

### Naked *p*-value

❌ *"The intervention significantly reduced infection (p < 0.05)."*

::: {.fragment}
✅ *"…reduced surgical-site infection by 6.2 points (12.1% vs 18.3%; RR 0.66, 95% CI 0.48–0.91; *P* = 0.01)."*
:::
:::

:::{.aside}
Phase 2 Part A · Editage · Enago.
:::

## ⚡ Activity 1 — "Where does it go?" {.smaller}

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
I read a scenario — you **shout** `TEXT! / TABLE! / FIGURE!` <br>
No groups, no devices. First instinct.
:::

. . .

I read; you call it out:

1.  A single overall prevalence
2.  Baseline characteristics, 12 variables × 2 groups
3.  Survival over 24 months by arm
4.  Participant flow
5.  Distribution of CRP in 30 patients
6.  Three subgroup odds ratios *(deliberately ambiguous)*

. . .

Then **fix the sentence**: *"significant (p<0.05)"* · *"smoking caused lower birthweight"* (cross-sectional).

## Activity 1 — answer key {.smaller}

| # | Scenario | Home |
|:--|:---|:---|
| 1 | Single prevalence | **Text** |
| 2 | Baseline characteristics | **Table** |
| 3 | Survival by arm | **Figure** — K–M |
| 4 | Participant flow | **Figure** — flow diagram |
| 5 | CRP in 30 patients | **Figure** — dot/box, **not** bar |
| 6 | Three subgroup ORs | **Table *or* forest plot** |

. . .

-   *"p<0.05"* = **naked p-value** · *"caused"* = **causal language** (cross-sectional)

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
**#5** is the trap — a bar chart for 30 values hides the distribution. **#6** has no single right answer — pick by audience.
:::

# Block 2 {.inverse background-color="#1f5560"}

### Table & figure principles, and which figure fits which design

## Table 1 reports distribution-appropriate summaries — by variable type {.smaller}

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
-   Continuous, symmetric → **mean ± SD**
-   Continuous, skewed → **median (IQR)**
-   Categorical → **n (%)** with denominator
-   Title **above** · footnotes **below**
-   Abbreviations defined · **no vertical rules**
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
| Characteristic | Arm A (n=105) | Arm B (n=108) |
|:---|:--:|:--:|
| Age, yr — mean ± SD | 54 ± 11 | 55 ± 10 |
| LOS, d — median (IQR) | 8 (5–12) | 9 (6–13) |
| Diabetes — n (%) | 31 (29.5) | 29 (26.9) |
:::
:::::

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Don't put **mean ± SD** on length-of-stay — it is always right-skewed.
:::

:::{.aside}
AMA 11th ed. · CONSORT Item 15 · STROBE Item 14.
:::

## *P*-values in Table 1 — no for RCTs, yes-ish for observational

::: panel-tabset
### RCT

-   **NO** baseline *p*-values
-   Randomisation handles balance by design
-   Any baseline difference **is** a chance difference — testing it answers a question no one asked
-   *CONSORT discourages it*

### Observational

-   Groups **self-select** → show comparability
-   Use a **standardised mean difference (SMD)** or a group comparison
-   Interpret as **balance**, not hypothesis-testing
:::

::: {.important}
The single most common Table 1 error in resident **RCT** manuscripts.
:::

:::{.aside}
CONSORT 2010 Item 15 (E&E) · STROBE.
:::

## Match the figure type to the study design {.smaller}

| Design | Key figures |
|:---|:---|
| **All** | Participant flow diagram |
| Cross-sectional | Ordered bar · prevalence map · forest (aOR) |
| Case-control | Forest (OR) · exposure distribution |
| Cohort | K–M · incidence · forest (subgroups) |
| Diagnostic | STARD flow · ROC · dot plot by status |
| RCT | CONSORT flow · K–M · forest · NNT |
| Syst. review | PRISMA flow · forest · funnel |

. . .

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
The **flow diagram** is the one universal. A K–M curve makes no sense for a cross-sectional study; an ROC belongs to diagnostic work. Find your row — that's your shortlist.
:::

:::{.aside}
Synthesis 2 · CONSORT/STROBE/STARD/PRISMA conventions.
:::

## Maximise data-ink — if you squint, the message should survive

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Remove**

-   3-D, exploding slices
-   gridlines, heavy borders
-   redundant legends
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Keep**

-   the data
-   direct labels
-   the **one** key finding
:::
:::::

. . .

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
**The squint test** — blur your eyes; if the main message disappears, the figure is too busy. Build figures in R and you get clean defaults for free.
:::

:::{.aside}
Tufte, *Visual Display of Quantitative Information* · Schriger & Cooper, Ann Emerg Med 2001.
:::

## For continuous data, dot/box plots beat bar charts

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
-   Bars hide the **distribution** and **n**
-   Wildly different data → **identical** bars
-   Show every point when n is small
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
A five-minute change in `ggplot`:

`geom_jitter()` + a median crossbar instead of `geom_col()` + error bar.
:::
:::
:::::

::: {.important}
Different datasets can produce the same bar-and-error-bar chart — the bar hides everything.
:::

:::{.aside}
Weissgerber TL et al., PLOS Biology 2015;13(4):e1002128 (CC-BY).
:::

## ⚡ Activity 2 — "Pick the figure" then "Spot the table crime" {.smaller}

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
**Part A** — 5 scenarios → name the best figure. **Part B** — spot the crimes in one bad table. Shout it out.
:::

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Part A**

1.  Survival by arm over 3 years
2.  Sens/spec across thresholds
3.  Eight subgroup hazard ratios
4.  Flow of 1,200 screened
5.  District anaemia prevalence
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Part B — name the crimes**

-   no title · "Group 1/2" headers
-   mixed mean/median, unlabelled
-   inconsistent decimals
-   internal vertical rules
-   undefined "DM"
-   *p*-values on RCT baseline
:::
:::::

## Activity 2 — answer key {.smaller}

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Part A**

1.  K–M curve
2.  ROC curve
3.  Forest plot
4.  CONSORT flow
5.  Ordered bar / map *(not pie)*
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Part B — crimes**

no title · vague headers · mixed/unlabelled summaries · inconsistent decimals · vertical rules · undefined abbrev · **RCT baseline *p*-values**
:::
:::::

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
Figure type **follows design** (A); a table must be **self-contained & design-correct** (B). The RCT-baseline *p*-value is the gotcha — callback to two slides ago.
:::

# Block 3 {.inverse background-color="#1f5560"}

### Same question, different design, different Results

## Same question, different design, different Results {.smaller}

Legend: ✓✓ critical · ✓ common · — n/a

| Results element | Cross-sec | Case-ctrl | Cohort | Diagnostic | RCT |
|:---|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|
| Prevalence + 95% CI | ✓✓ | — | ~ | — | — |
| Odds ratio (adj.) | ✓ | ✓✓ | — | — | — |
| Risk / hazard ratio | ~ | — | ✓✓ | — | ✓ |
| Sens / spec · ROC · 2×2 | — | — | — | ✓✓ | — |
| ITT + NNT + harms | — | — | — | — | ✓✓ |
| Person-time / follow-up | — | — | ✓✓ | — | ~ |

. . .

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
Find your column. The same clinical question, asked under a different design, gives a **different Results section**.
:::

## Observational Results: prevalence, odds, person-time {.smaller}

::: panel-tabset
### Cross-sectional

-   **Prevalence + 95% CI**; adjusted ORs (aOR)
-   **Weights / design effect** if clustered (NFHS-style)
-   Say *"associated with"* — **never** *"caused"*

### Case-control

-   **Odds ratios**, not risk ratios
-   Matched design → **conditional logistic** (matched OR)
-   Report exposure distribution by case/control

### Cohort

-   **Person-time**, incidence rates
-   **Follow-up completeness & attrition** before the HR
-   HR + CI · K–M · acknowledge **competing risks**
:::

:::{.aside}
STROBE design-specific items.
:::

## Diagnostic Results: the 2×2, accuracy with CIs, and the ROC {.smaller}

::::: columns
::: {.column width="48%"}
|  | Disease + | Disease − |
|:--|:--:|:--:|
| **Test +** | TP | FP |
| **Test −** | FN | TN |
:::

::: {.column width="52%"}
-   Sens, Spec, PPV, NPV, LR± — **all with 95% CI**
-   **ROC + AUC** — the sens/spec trade-off
-   Report **indeterminate / failed** tests
-   **STARD flow** accounts for everyone
:::
:::::

::: {.important}
Give the 2×2 explicitly so the reader can recompute anything. Accuracy varies with disease spectrum — report across it.
:::

:::{.aside}
STARD 2015 (2×2, flow, accuracy items).
:::

## RCT Results: CONSORT flow, ITT first, absolute + relative, harms {.smaller}

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
-   **CONSORT flow** + **CTRI** number
-   **ITT** primary; per-protocol = sensitivity
-   Report **absolute + relative** effect; NNT
-   **Harms** table · NI margin if applicable
-   **No** baseline *p*-values
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
### RECOVERY (NEJM 2021)
99.6% follow-up · rate ratio **0.83 (0.75–0.93)** · subgroup forest plot · harms reported · **zero interpretation** in Results.
:::
:::
:::::

::: {.important}
A 2.8-point **absolute** reduction means more clinically than a bare relative risk. Indian trials must be **CTRI-registered** — editors look for it.
:::

:::{.aside}
CONSORT 2010 Items 13–19 · RECOVERY, NEJM 2021;384:693–704.
:::

## One question, four designs, four Results paragraphs {.smaller}

> **Q: Is diabetes associated with surgical-site infection?**

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Cross-sectional** <br> prevalence of SSI by diabetes status; **aOR + CI**

**Case-control** <br> odds of diabetes in SSI cases vs controls; **OR + CI**
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Cohort** <br> incidence over person-time; **HR + CI**; K–M

**RCT** (glucose-control) <br> CONSORT flow; **ITT risk difference + NNT**
:::
:::::

. . .

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
The clinical question never moved; the **design dictated the Results**. This is the slide to remember.
:::

:::{.aside}
Synthesis 2 · designed cross-department example.
:::

## Your one-page Results checklist {.smaller}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
### Universal — every paper
flow first · one home per finding · effect + CI + exact *P* · self-contained displays · cite every item in order · all pre-specified outcomes · **no interpretation**
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
### By design
Cross-sec → prevalence + CI, aOR · Case-control → OR, matched · Cohort → person-time, HR · Diagnostic → 2×2, ROC, indeterminate · RCT → CONSORT + CTRI, ITT, NNT, harms
:::

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
**Resources** — EQUATOR-network.org · SAMPL (Lang & Altman) · Editage Insights · Enago Academy · AuthorAID
:::
